description:
Verified on origin/main a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83.

## Goal

Every direct return edge inside one recursion component must use one physical
return layout, including callable-demand returns, without erasing the exact
callable identity preserved by the singleton recursive `make/1` case.

## Live repro

    fn left(0), do: fn (x) -> x + 1 end
    fn left(n), do: right(n - 1)
    fn right(0), do: fn (x) -> x + 2 end
    fn right(n), do: left(n - 1)

    fn main() do
      f = left(3)
      dbg(f.(40))
    end

The current backend artifact gives `left/1` and `right/1` the same semantic return
type:

    closure[left_lambda]() | closure[right_lambda]()

and the same callable runtime demand containing both targets, but publishes
different return layouts:

    left/1  = callable(<unknown>/0), carrier=ValueRef
    right/1 = callable(right_lambda/1), carrier=ValueRef

Both recursive return-position calls are therefore `Continue` rather than `Tail`:

    left -> right = Continue
    right -> left = Continue

## Root cause

`produce_named_transport_position` computes `cycle_return` only when
`!demand.is_callable()`, so callable returns bypass `contract_transport_layout`.
The structural cut then resolves the two sides independently. The cut-side
`right/1` sees only its local lambda evidence; `cut_transport_layout` accepts that
form because `shape_carries` treats any callable shape as carrying the callable
type. The surviving `left/1` side sees both distinct lambda forms, joins them,
and falls back to a generic boxed callable. Artifact sealing correctly refuses
`Tail` because source, payload, and caller-return layouts disagree.

## Signal / red-first gate

Add the repro above to transport-contract coverage and assert:

1. both in-component direct calls are `BackendReturnFlow::Tail`;
2. `left/1` and `right/1` publish identical `BackendReturnLayout`s;
3. execution still returns `42` on interp, JIT, and AOT.

The existing `compiler2_one_recursion_component_publishes_one_return_contract`
test states this invariant but its 00420 fixture exercises only data returns,
so it does not bind the callable carve-out.

## Non-regression constraint

`compiler2_transport_plan_preserves_recursive_callable_return_identity` must
remain green. Its singleton `make(n) -> make(n - 1)` cycle must keep a resolved
local callable target rather than being replaced unconditionally by a generic
boxed callable.

## Strategy

Make the recursion contract callable-aware. Derive one agreed form from the
component's callable demand:

- preserve the exact callable form when every demanded target names one
  physical `CallableDescr`;
- otherwise use the generic boxed callable form shared by every return,
  `ReturnPayload`, and caller-return endpoint.

Do not force today's generic contract unconditionally: that previously erased
the exact singleton `make/1` identity.

## Closure-carried residual

`TransportRecipe::ClosureCallReturn` still deliberately cuts its grounded edge
without reporting `on_cycle`. Existing `closure_threaded_recursion` fixtures now
measure these cycles on all three execution paths, and the current data fixture
has agreeing `RawInt` returns and a tail grounded closure call. No disagreeing
data-return reproduction was established in this audit. Keep that possibility
out of this ticket unless a red fixture demonstrates it; file it separately if
one is found.
title: Callable returns in a direct recursion component bypass the one-return-contract rule and demote both edges to Continue
